front: Two learning principles behind the final-review routine?
back: Retrieval practice (recalling beats re-reading) and spacing (reviews spread over days beat cramming).

front: Sensible maximum number of full mocks in the final two weeks at ~1.5 h/day?
back: About five, each with a 20–30 minute self-review. The review is where the learning happens.

front: When should the last full mock be?
back: Around D-3, so its review can still change something. D-1 stays light.

front: What makes a quiz topic a weak spot?
back: Under 70% correct over the section's last two quiz attempts.

front: What makes a section a stale weak spot?
back: With a plan start date set, its checkpoints are untouched 14+ days after its plan week ended.

front: Why retake a weak-spot quiz the next day, not immediately?
back: The score rests on about 4 answers, so one memorised retake clears it. A retake a day later is real retrieval.

front: SM-2 intervals for a new card graded Good?
back: 1 day, then 6 days, then about 15 days (6 × default ease 2.5).

front: What does grading a card Again do?
back: Restarts it: back tomorrow, one more lapse counted.

front: Last useful day to add new flashcards, and why?
back: About D-8: its 6-day review still lands on D-1. A card added later gets only two reviews (the day added and the next day) before the interview.

front: Due count too high late in prep?
back: Lower 'New cards / day' for a few days; don't skip due reviews, which pile up.

front: Rule before redoing a failed simulator challenge?
back: Say the mechanism and your prediction out loud first, then run it. A wrong prediction is the gap to fix.

front: Which mocks to redo in the final weeks?
back: Your lowest recent case (after 3–4 days), at least two unseen cases, and cases that stress your weak deep dives.
Mock: timed, no pause, each hint costs one rubric point. Practice: pause any time, free hints, deep dives on request.

front: What does the dashboard interview trend show, and what does it leave out?
back: Self-score % per attempt per case (Mock hint penalty included), oldest to newest, plus the change from first to latest. It leaves out how much of a rise is memory of a repeated case.

front: Why is a rising score on a repeated case weak evidence?
back: Memory of the case inflates it. Unseen cases test whether the skill transfers.
20–30 min, done 30+ min before: one estimation drill, the framework out loud, one deep-dive answer out loud, a glance at the checklist.
